ble_219_0c031d78.name: hal_spi_apply_format
ble_219_0c031d78.summary: Load SPI frame-format word and extra byte config into an SPI instance
ble_219_0c031d78.description: Looks up the SPI register block for instance param_1 in the pointer table at 0x0c08425c and writes two values from a config struct: the 32-bit word goes to register +0x00 (CR0, frame format/clock fields) and a byte goes to register +0x88 (BES-specific extension register). param_3 selects between two sub-records of the config: 0 uses word at param_2+0x0 and byte at param_2+0xc, non-zero uses word at param_2+0x4 and byte at param_2+0xd. Table at 0x0c08425c holds the register-block base pointers of the SPI instances; register layout matches an ARM PrimeCell PL022 SSP (CR0 +0, CR1 +4, DR +8, SR +0xc, ICR +0x20) with a BES extension at +0x88. Called from SPI open/configure routines and from the transfer wrapper at 0x0c0460e8.

params.name: param_1
params.description: SPI instance index into the register-pointer table

params.name: param_2
params.description: config struct holding the two (word, byte) records

ble_219_0c031d78.notes: Which two records the config holds (e.g. master vs slave / two chip-select profiles) is not visible from this function; the semantics of register +0x88 are undocumented.

ble_219_0c032288.name: hal_spi_txrx_poll
ble_219_0c032288.summary: Polled full-duplex SPI transfer of N bytes using an 8-deep FIFO window
ble_219_0c032288.description: Derives the frame size in bits from ((param_2 & 0x1fffff) >> 16) + 1 and maps it to an element width of 1 (<=8 bits), 2 (<=16 bits) or 4 bytes; returns -1 if param_5 (byte count) is zero or not a multiple of the element width. Returns -11 (0xfffffff5) if the SPI status register (+0xc) BSY bit4 is set, otherwise waits for SR bit2 to clear, clears all interrupt flags (ICR +0x20 = 0xffffffff) and runs a loop: while the enable/active flag (reg +4 bit1) is set it pushes the next tx element into DR (+8) when SR bit1 (TX not full) is set, never more than 8 bytes ahead of what was received, using zero as dummy data when param_3 (tx buffer) is NULL, and pops an element from DR into param_4 (rx buffer, must be non-NULL) when SR bit2 (RX not empty) is set. On completion it waits for the busy/active state to end. Table at 0x0c08425c holds the register-block base pointers of the SPI instances; register layout matches an ARM PrimeCell PL022 SSP (CR0 +0, CR1 +4, DR +8, SR +0xc, ICR +0x20) with a BES extension at +0x88.

params.name: param_2
params.description: SPI format/CR0 value; bits 20:16 give frame size minus one

params.name: param_3
params.description: tx buffer or NULL for dummy zero data

returns.description: 0 = all bytes exchanged, 1 = transfer ended early (active flag dropped), -1 = bad length/alignment, -11 = SPI busy

ble_219_0c032288.notes: Meaning of register +4 bit1 as a loop-continue flag (PL022 CR1.SSE) and the return value 1 are inferred from the control flow.

ble_219_0c032378.name: hal_spi_tx_poll
ble_219_0c032378.summary: Polled transmit-only SPI transfer of N bytes
ble_219_0c032378.description: Same frame-size decoding and argument validation as the full-duplex routine (element width 1/2/4 bytes from bits 20:16 of param_2; returns -1 if length is 0 or not width-aligned). Loops while the active flag (reg +4 bit1) is set and bytes remain, writing the next element to DR (+8) whenever SR (+0xc) bit1 (TX not full) is set; received data is not read. After the loop it waits until reg+4 bit1 clears or SR bit4 (BSY) drops, and returns 1 if not all bytes were sent else 0. Table at 0x0c08425c holds the register-block base pointers of the SPI instances; register layout matches an ARM PrimeCell PL022 SSP (CR0 +0, CR1 +4, DR +8, SR +0xc, ICR +0x20) with a BES extension at +0x88.

params.name: param_2
params.description: SPI format/CR0 value; bits 20:16 give frame size minus one

ble_219_0c0326a8.name: hal_periph_9000_set_field_10_7
ble_219_0c0326a8.summary: Set a 4-bit field (bits 10:7) in the register at 0x40009004
ble_219_0c0326a8.description: Read-modify-write of 0x40009004: clears bits 10:7 (mask 0xfffff87f) and ORs in param_1 << 7. Values >= 15 are rejected by spinning forever (assert-style trap). Called three times from the 0x0c0401b0-0x0c040378 group; the register block at 0x40009000 is BES-specific and undocumented, the field looks like a divider/selector index 0..14.
ble_219_0c0326a8.notes: Peripheral identity of 0x40009000 is unknown; the divider/selector interpretation is a guess.

ble_219_0c032d64.name: hal_cmu_get_freq_name
ble_219_0c032d64.summary: Map a CMU frequency index (0..7) to its name string
ble_219_0c032d64.description: Returns the entry at index param_1 of the pointer table at 0x0c080924 whose strings are "CMU_FREQ_32K", "CMU_FREQ_6P5M", "CMU_FREQ_13M", "CMU_FREQ_26M", "CMU_FREQ_52M", "CMU_FREQ_78M", "CMU_FREQ_104M", "CMU_FREQ_208M"; returns NULL for index >= 8. Used for trace output of the system clock selection (single caller 0x0c0459fc).
ble_219_0c032d64.notes: Function name is derived (BES SDK style) - the string table is the evidence.

ble_219_0c033030.name: hal_sys_timer_delay_us
ble_219_0c033030.summary: Busy-wait for param_1 microseconds on the hardware tick counter
ble_219_0c033030.description: Converts param_1 to float, computes ticks = (us / 1000.0) * DAT_20003548 + 0.99 where DAT_20003548 holds ticks per millisecond, then samples the free-running counter at 0x40002004 and spins until (start - now) is no longer below the tick count (counter counts downward / difference taken unsigned). Negative or zero tick counts return immediately. Always returns 0. Callers are the BLE controller code at 0x0c030ab0/0x0c030cb8 and the delay at 0x0c033328.
ble_219_0c033030.notes: Direction of the counter at 0x40002004 is inferred from the (start - now) comparison.

ble_219_0c03308c.name: hal_sys_timer_alarm_start
ble_219_0c03308c.summary: Arm the 0x4000200x timer for a one-shot wake after param_1 ticks
ble_219_0c03308c.description: Clamps the tick count: values 0 and 1 become 1, larger values become param_1 - 1. Saves the negated current counter (0x40002004) into DAT_20003c10 as the reference for later elapsed-time reads, writes the clamped value to the load register 0x40002020 and sets bit7 (enable) in the control register 0x40002028. Counterparts: stop at 0x0c0330b8, elapsed at 0x0c0330fc.

params.name: param_1
params.description: timer ticks until the alarm fires

ble_219_0c0330b8.name: hal_sys_timer_alarm_stop
ble_219_0c0330b8.summary: Stop the alarm timer and clear its pending interrupt
ble_219_0c0330b8.description: Clears bit7 (enable) in 0x40002028, writes 1 to 0x4000202c (interrupt acknowledge) and writes 0x2000 to NVIC ICPR0 (0xe000e280), clearing the pending state of IRQ 13. Complements the alarm start at 0x0c03308c.

ble_219_0c0330e0.name: hal_sys_timer_alarm_is_running
ble_219_0c0330e0.summary: Return whether the alarm timer enable bit is set
ble_219_0c0330e0.description: Reads control register 0x40002028 and returns bit7 (value 0 or 1), the enable flag that the alarm start routine sets and the stop routine clears.

returns.description: 1 if the alarm is armed, else 0

ble_219_0c0330f0.name: hal_sys_timer_alarm_get_count
ble_219_0c0330f0.summary: Read the alarm timer current-value register
ble_219_0c0330f0.description: Returns the raw 32-bit value of register 0x40002024 (current/remaining count of the alarm timer whose load register is 0x40002020).

ble_219_0c0330fc.name: hal_sys_timer_alarm_elapsed
ble_219_0c0330fc.summary: Ticks elapsed on the free-running counter since the alarm was armed
ble_219_0c0330fc.description: Computes -(counter + DAT_20003c10), where counter is the register at 0x40002004 and DAT_20003c10 holds the negated counter value stored when the alarm was started, i.e. start_value - current_value, giving elapsed ticks of a down-counting timer.

ble_219_0c033d18.name: hal_uart_putc_poll
ble_219_0c033d18.summary: Write one byte to a UART transmit register, waiting for FIFO space
ble_219_0c033d18.description: param_1 selects one of 3 UART instances (register-block pointers in a table at 0x0c085890, stride 12 bytes); larger values trap in an infinite loop. Spins until flag register +0x18 bit5 (TXFF, PL011 layout) is clear, then, if bit1 of register +0x48 is not set, stores param_2 into the data register (+0x00); if that bit is set (probably TX DMA active) the code traps in an infinite loop. Used by the trace/print path (0x0c045ac8, 0x0c033150).
ble_219_0c033d18.notes: Offset +0x48 bit1 meaning (DMA enable) is a guess; layout is PL011-like.

ble_219_0c033d50.name: hal_uart_set_irq_mask
ble_219_0c033d50.summary: Write the UART interrupt mask register and return its previous value
ble_219_0c033d50.description: param_1 selects UART 0..2 from the table at 0x0c085890 (otherwise trap). Reads the old value of register +0x38 (PL011 IMSC), then writes param_2. If bit6 (receive timeout) is being newly enabled while the per-UART DMA channel slot DAT_2000aa8c[param_1] is not -1 (i.e. an RX DMA is configured) the function traps in an infinite loop as an assertion. Returns the old mask.
ble_219_0c033d50.notes: Meaning of DAT_2000aa8c as an RX DMA channel array (-1 = none) is inferred.

ble_219_0c033d94.name: hal_uart_install_irq_handler
ble_219_0c033d94.summary: Store UART callback, argument and ISR entry for instance param_1
ble_219_0c033d94.description: For instance 0..2 (else infinite-loop trap) stores param_2 into the word array at 0x2000aaac, param_3 into the byte array at 0x2000aac8 and writes the address of the code at 0x0c033c34 (the common UART interrupt service routine) into the 4-byte-entry handler table at 0x2000aa80. No direct callers - invoked indirectly during UART open.

params.name: param_2
params.description: callback / context value stored per instance

params.name: param_3
params.description: small per-instance value stored in a byte array (low byte only)

ble_219_0c033d94.notes: Exact roles of param_2/param_3 are not clear; entry reached via function pointer.

ble_219_0c0342b8.name: hal_irq_get_handler_table
ble_219_0c0342b8.summary: Return the base address of the RAM handler table at 0x2000aa80
ble_219_0c0342b8.description: Returns the constant pointer 0x2000aa80, the table of 4-byte ISR entry addresses that the UART install routine (0x0c033d94) fills. Single caller 0x0c0467b8.

ble_219_0c0342d4.name: hal_wdt_write_load
ble_219_0c0342d4.summary: Write the stored reload value of watchdog param_1 to the watchdog LOAD register
ble_219_0c0342d4.description: Runs in a critical section by raising BASEPRI to 0x40; if it was not already 0x40 it records the caller PC and LR in DAT_20003d70/20003d74 (lock-owner debug record) and, when BASEPRI was originally 0, resets DAT_20003d70 to 0xffffffff on exit; the previous BASEPRI is restored. Unlocks the block by writing 0x1acce551 to 0x40082c00, stores the value from table DAT_2000aad4[param_1] into 0x40082000 (LOAD) and relocks by writing 1 to 0x40082c00. SP805-style watchdog block at 0x40082000: LOAD +0x00, CONTROL +0x08, LOCK +0xc00 (0x1acce551 unlocks). Called from the watchdog start/feed routines (0x0c034328, 0x0c046830).

params.name: param_1
params.description: watchdog index into the timeout table at 0x2000aad4

ble_219_0c0342d4.notes: Identification as an SP805 watchdog is based on the 0x1acce551 unlock key and register offsets.

ble_219_0c034388.name: hal_wdt_stop
ble_219_0c034388.summary: Disable the watchdog counter and clear the running flag
ble_219_0c034388.description: Runs in a critical section by raising BASEPRI to 0x40; if it was not already 0x40 it records the caller PC and LR in DAT_20003d70/20003d74 (lock-owner debug record) and, when BASEPRI was originally 0, resets DAT_20003d70 to 0xffffffff on exit; the previous BASEPRI is restored. Unlocks 0x40082c00 with 0x1acce551, writes 0 to 0x40082008 (CONTROL: counter and reset disabled), relocks with 1, then clears the running flag DAT_2000aadc. SP805-style watchdog block at 0x40082000: LOAD +0x00, CONTROL +0x08, LOCK +0xc00 (0x1acce551 unlocks).

ble_219_0c03442c.name: hal_wdt_irq_enable
ble_219_0c03442c.summary: Install watchdog IRQ vector and callback, then enable NVIC IRQ 5
ble_219_0c03442c.description: Reads VTOR (0xe000ed08) and copies the handler address from table DAT_20003e28[param_1] into vector slot 0x54 (exception 21 = IRQ 5), issues a DSB, sets NVIC priority byte 0xe000e405 (IRQ5) to 0, clears pending (ICPR 0xe000e280 = 0x20) and enables the interrupt (ISER 0xe000e100 = 0x20). Finally stores the callback param_2 in DAT_2000aad8[param_1]. IRQ 5 is presumed to be the watchdog interrupt, matching the SP805 block used by neighbouring routines.

params.name: param_1
params.description: index into handler table 0x20003e28 and callback table 0x2000aad8

params.name: param_2
params.description: callback invoked from the watchdog interrupt

ble_219_0c034818.name: bes_image_format_name
ble_219_0c034818.summary: Return a name string for a section image-format magic value
ble_219_0c034818.description: Maps a 32-bit ASCII magic to a text label: 0x4d494152 ("RAIM") -> "romfs", 0x20574152 ("RAW ") -> "raw", 0x34574152 ("RAW4") -> "raw4k", 0x50495a47 ("GZIP") -> "gzip", anything else -> "unknwon" (sic, typo in firmware). Used by the code at 0x0c03655c/0x0c0365a4 when printing the format of an image/partition record.
ble_219_0c034818.notes: Calling context (boot image / romfs section dump) inferred from the labels only.

ble_219_0c035684.name: hal_trace_buf_putc
ble_219_0c035684.summary: Append a byte to a line buffer and flush through a write callback when full
ble_219_0c035684.description: param_1 points to an output-stream object: write callback at +0x50, capacity (u16) at +0x54, fill count (u16) at +0x56, buffer pointer at +0x58. If room remains, stores param_2 at buffer[fill++]; returns 0 if still not full. When the buffer is full (or already was) and non-empty, repeatedly calls the callback with the buffer (the decompiler shows only the buffer pointer as argument, the length presumably in r1), advancing by the number of bytes consumed and decreasing the fill count, until the buffer is empty; a negative callback result is returned immediately. Returns the total bytes flushed.

params.name: param_1
params.description: output stream object (callback +0x50, capacity +0x54, count +0x56, buffer +0x58)

returns.description: 0 if only buffered, bytes flushed on flush, or negative error from the callback

ble_219_0c035684.notes: Three callers at 0x0c0356dc, 0x0c0357b8 and 0x0c035900 (print formatting path).

ble_219_0c035f90.name: Default_Handler
ble_219_0c035f90.summary: Fallback exception handler: dump fault registers and halt
ble_219_0c035f90.description: Selects the stacked exception frame by EXC_RETURN bit2 (MSP or PSP), clears the 0x100-byte buffer at 0x2000b9a4 with memset, copies SCB registers SHCSR/CFSR/HFSR/MMFAR/BFAR/AFSR (0xe000ed24..ed3c) to 0x2000b9f0..ba04 and the stacked R0-R3, R12, LR, PC, xPSR to 0x2000ba08..ba24. It then prints "start backtrace:\r\n" byte-wise via the trace UART putc (0x0c045ac8), formats "pc:0x%x,lr:0x%x \r\n" with the stacked PC/LR using the snprintf at 0x0c071570 and prints that, calls the crash-dump routine 0x0c0476a0 (&0x0c0809a4, 0x2000b9ac, 0x78, 1), and spins forever. Installed on vector slot 13 (reserved); the body is identical to HardFault_Handler.

ble_219_0c035fa8.name: HardFault_Handler
ble_219_0c035fa8.summary: HardFault handler: dump fault state to trace UART and halt
ble_219_0c035fa8.description: Selects the stacked exception frame by EXC_RETURN bit2 (MSP or PSP), clears the 0x100-byte buffer at 0x2000b9a4 with memset, copies SCB registers SHCSR/CFSR/HFSR/MMFAR/BFAR/AFSR (0xe000ed24..ed3c) to 0x2000b9f0..ba04 and the stacked R0-R3, R12, LR, PC, xPSR to 0x2000ba08..ba24. It then prints "start backtrace:\r\n" byte-wise via the trace UART putc (0x0c045ac8), formats "pc:0x%x,lr:0x%x \r\n" with the stacked PC/LR using the snprintf at 0x0c071570 and prints that, calls the crash-dump routine 0x0c0476a0 (&0x0c0809a4, 0x2000b9ac, 0x78, 1), and spins forever.

ble_219_0c035fe8.name: _fstat
ble_219_0c035fe8.summary: newlib stub fstat reporting every descriptor as a character device
ble_219_0c035fe8.description: Sets st->st_mode (offset 4 of the stat struct in param_2) to 0x2000 (S_IFCHR) and returns 0. Part of the newlib syscall stubs for the retargeted stdio; referenced from an indirect table at 0x0c073a8c.

ble_219_0c035ff4.name: _isatty
ble_219_0c035ff4.summary: newlib stub isatty that always reports a terminal
ble_219_0c035ff4.description: Ignores its arguments and returns 1, so stdio treats all file descriptors as interactive (line buffered). Referenced from the syscall table around 0x0c073a88.

ble_219_0c036024.name: util_ctz32
ble_219_0c036024.summary: Count trailing zero bits of a 32-bit word (returns 32 for 0)
ble_219_0c036024.description: Binary-search count of trailing zeros: returns 32 for 0 and 0 when bit0 is set; otherwise tests the low 16/8/4/2 bits in turn, shifting and accumulating the index, and finally subtracts bit0 of the remainder. Result is the zero-based index of the lowest set bit. Sole caller 0x0c02dea8.

ble_219_0c0360c8.description: Does nothing and returns 0; reached from a callback or hook-table call site at 0x0c05f338 where the default behaviour is success/false.

ble_219_0c0360cc.name: stub_return_zero_0c0360cc

ble_219_0c036388.name: hal_trace_set_flag_baa4
ble_219_0c036388.summary: Set the global flag at 0x2000baa4 to 1
ble_219_0c036388.description: Writes 1 into DAT_2000baa4 and returns. No direct callers - invoked through a function pointer/hook. The flag is later copied out by the accessor at 0x0c0363a4.
ble_219_0c036388.notes: Role of the flag is unknown; it sits next to the crash/trace RAM variables (0x2000b9xx..baxx) so it may be a crash/trace state indicator.

ble_219_0c0363a4.name: hal_trace_get_state_vars
ble_219_0c0363a4.summary: Copy three global words (0x2000baac, baa8, baa4) to caller-provided pointers
ble_219_0c0363a4.description: If param_1 and param_2 are both non-NULL, stores DAT_2000baac to *param_1, DAT_2000baa8 to *param_2 and DAT_2000baa4 to *param_3 (param_3 is not NULL-checked); otherwise does nothing. No direct callers - reached indirectly.
ble_219_0c0363a4.notes: Semantics of the three values unknown.

ble_219_0c036418.name: crypto_tea_cbc_decrypt
ble_219_0c036418.summary: TEA (32-round) decryption of a buffer in place with CBC-style chaining
ble_219_0c036418.description: Requires param_2 (byte length) to be a multiple of 8, otherwise returns -1. For each 8-byte block it decrypts with standard TEA decryption: 32 rounds, delta 0x9e3779b9 (sum starts at 0xc6ef3720), key words k0..k3 read from param_5[0..3]. If the running byte counter *param_3 is non-zero, the plaintext is XORed with the previous ciphertext block held in the 8-byte chain buffer param_4; the chain buffer is then replaced by the block's ciphertext and *param_3 is advanced by 8. A leading loop over (*param_3 >> 10) and a per-block loop run byte additions on an uninitialised local array whose result is never used (dead code). Returns 0 on success. Caller 0x0c0285ec.

params.name: param_2
params.description: length in bytes, must be a multiple of 8

params.name: param_3
params.description: u32 running byte offset; first block (0) is not chained, advanced by 8 per block

returns.description: 0 on success, -1 if length not a multiple of 8

ble_219_0c036418.notes: Likely used to decrypt firmware-update or config data; the caller context was not examined.

ble_219_0c03a80c.name: memcpy_newlib_aligned_16
ble_219_0c03a80c.summary: newlib memcpy: copy param_3 bytes from param_2 to param_1
ble_219_0c03a80c.description: newlib-style optimised memcpy. For lengths below 16 or when source and destination alignments differ (low two bits of src^dst), it copies byte by byte. Otherwise it copies bytes until the destination is word-aligned, then 16 bytes per iteration as four words, then remaining whole words, then the trailing bytes. The decompiler shows no return value but newlib returns the destination pointer in r0. Caller 0x0c03cec8.
